comments.author: @John_Doe____
comments.text: To add some context regarding Japanese emigration: in the past, the Japanese government—seeking to alleviate overpopulation caused by famine—recruited impoverished farmers for migration to Brazil using false information, only to subsequently abandon them. Today, Japan, in need of a low-cost labor force, accepts the descendants of these Japanese emigrants from Brazil; however, Japanese society views them as "Brazilians" and denies them any rights as Japanese citizens.

comments.text: Fun fact:  although Brazil doesn't have a border with Ecuador, it has a border TREATY with Ecuador. To make a long story short, Peru and Ecuador have a VERY longstanding territorial dispute, so at the beginning of the 20th Century Brazil negotiated the same border with both countries, so that whoever ended up the the territory on the other side, Brazil's border would not be affected.
